events.title: Battle of Morgarten
events.description: Swiss Confederates ambushed and defeated a larger Habsburg army led by Duke Leopold I at the Morgarten pass, using the terrain to their advantage against heavily armored knights.
events.significance: The victory strengthened the early Swiss Confederacy and is regarded as a foundational moment in Swiss independence and the reputation of Swiss infantry.

events.title: Articles of Confederation Adopted by the Continental Congress
events.description: The Second Continental Congress approved the Articles of Confederation and sent them to the states for ratification, establishing a framework for a loose union of the thirteen states.
events.significance: The Articles served as the first constitution of the United States, and their weaknesses led to the drafting of the U.S. Constitution in 1787.

events.title: Brazil Becomes a Republic
events.description: A military coup led by Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca deposed Emperor Pedro II and proclaimed the Republic of the United States of Brazil, ending the Brazilian Empire.
events.significance: The event ended nearly 67 years of monarchy in Brazil and began the country's republican era.

events.title: Manhattan Project Scientists' Declaration and Trinity Aftermath: Truman, Attlee and King Issue Atomic Declaration
events.description: On November 15, 1945, U.S. President Harry Truman, British Prime Minister Clement Attlee and Canadian Prime Minister Mackenzie King issued a joint declaration on atomic energy, calling for international control and proposing a UN commission to address the dangers of nuclear weapons.
events.significance: The declaration was an early effort at nuclear arms control and led to the creation of the UN Atomic Energy Commission in 1946.

events.title: Intel Releases the 4004 Microprocessor
events.description: Intel publicly introduced the 4004, the first commercially available single-chip microprocessor, designed by Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff, Stanley Mazor, and Masatoshi Shima.
events.significance: The 4004 launched the microprocessor era, paving the way for personal computers and the modern digital revolution.
